lessonTitle: Council Chamber: Which Region Needs This Resource?
title: Dry Land Diorama
details: 📅 Q3 · Unit 8 · Synthesis 2: The Regional Council

badge.name: Council Ribbon
badge.line: Only VR curators earn this one. You followed the evidence to a dry place and told the truth about water.

hook.look: A work order is a note that tells museum workers what job to do next.
hook.head: Work Order 23 · Dry Land Diorama
rows: An old fort in the dry Southwest
hook.alt: Two satellite pictures of a lake. In the right picture, from 2022, the lake is much smaller.
hook.cap: Lake Mead from space, 2000 and 2022. It holds Colorado River water.
hook.note: The council wants to see a dry place up close. Please visit one and tell me about its water!

opti.brief: Curators, the council asked which region needs fresh water most. Visit an old fort in the dry Southwest, then record a short video.
opti.collections: No headset today? Come to the collections room. Play the game, then tell me what you found.

voice.brief: Curators, the council asked which region needs fresh water most. Visit an old fort in the dry Southwest, then record a short video.
voice.step1: Before your headset, read about the place. Then press Practice and say your two sentences before the timer ends.
voice.step2: Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type the map word, click the map, then click Begin Solo.
voice.step3: Move with the thumbstick. Walk around the fort. Look at the ground and the sky for clues that this place is dry.
voice.step4: Open Library, then Camera. Click Record video and say your two sentences. Click again to stop. Then send it on the Canvas tab.
voice.step5: Press the Meta button and click Quit. Then open the Canvas assignment and check that your video is there.
voice.extra: Have more time? Show the dry ground while you talk about water.
voice.collections: No headset today? Come to the collections room. Play the game, then tell me what you found.

vr.look: The Southwest is the driest region. The Alamo is an old fort in San Antonio, Texas, in the Southwest. Fresh water is water people can drink.

steps.title: Get ready
steps.html:
@PLACE@

In your video, you say these 2 sentences:

@SAY@

Practice now. Say both before the timer ends.

@TIMER@

In VR, this page is on the Canvas tab too.

steps.title: Go in
steps.html:
🔗 First time only: connect Canvas at xr.optimaed.com. See Having trouble in VR? below.

Open the On-Demand app. Click Explore. Type Alamo in Filter environments. Click The Alamo Fortress, then Begin Solo.

steps.title: Scout the fort
steps.html: Move with the thumbstick. Walk around the fort. Look at the ground and the sky for clues that this place is dry.

steps.title: Record your video and send it
steps.html:
Open your menu, click Library, then Camera. Move the tablet until the fort fits.

Click Record video. Say your 2 sentences. Click it again to stop.

Click the Canvas tab and pick @CANVAS@. Click Choose from My Files, pick your video, click Use this file, then Submit to Canvas. Look for the green Submitted tag.

🔁 Want to fix it? Record a new video and send it again.

steps.title: Check and leave
steps.html: Press the Meta button, then click Quit. Check that your video is in the Canvas assignment. Not there? Open Having trouble in VR?

extra.html: Point the camera down at the dry ground for a moment while you talk about water.

vr.full: One video, 30 seconds or less, that shows the fort while you say both sentences.

say: This old fort is in the Southwest, and I see ___.
The Southwest needs fresh water because ___.

studio.title: Water Evidence Map
studio.look: A simple map of the five regions of the United States. Each evidence card tells one true thing about land or water in one region.
studio.do: Read the card. Tap the region it belongs to, or drag the card onto the map.

game.miss: Not that region. Read the card again: where is this place?
game.done: The map is full. The Southwest is the driest region, so the evidence says it needs fresh water most.

cards.name: The Great Lakes
cards.what: Five huge lakes with about one fifth of the fresh water on top of the Earth.
cards.alt: Cliffs beside clear blue lake water
cards.ok: Yes! The Great Lakes sit on the Midwest. Lots of fresh water there.

cards.name: The Grand Canyon
cards.what: Dry land carved by the Colorado River. Very little rain falls here.
cards.ok: Yes! The Grand Canyon is in Arizona, in the dry Southwest.

cards.name: The Everglades
cards.what: A wide, wet grassland in Florida. Water moves slowly across it.
cards.ok: Yes! The Everglades are in Florida, in the Southeast. Plenty of rain there.

cards.name: Niagara Falls
cards.what: A giant waterfall between two of the Great Lakes, in New York.
cards.ok: Yes! Niagara Falls is in New York, in the Northeast. It has many rivers and lakes.

cards.name: Mount Rainier
cards.what: A snowy mountain in Washington, where many days bring gentle rain.
cards.alt: A snowy mountain by a lake
cards.ok: Yes! Mount Rainier is in Washington, in the West.

cards.name: Acoma Pueblo
cards.what: Adobe homes on dry land in New Mexico, under a deep blue sky.
cards.ok: Yes! Acoma Pueblo is in New Mexico, in the dry Southwest.

frames.lead: Which region needs fresh water most?
frames.starter: The region that needs fresh water most is ...

studio.full: All six cards are on the map, and your 2 sentences have 20 words or more.
